summary: Build board-level cyber oversight skills, interpret risk metrics, and strengthen incident readiness. Explore the two-day course and enquire.
lede: Board-level cybersecurity governance helps directors and senior executives oversee cyber risk, privacy, and digital resilience without taking on operational management. The course is for board members, executive leaders, and senior public-sector leaders who need to interpret risk indicators, challenge management reporting, assess third-party exposure, and review incident readiness. Exercises use NIST CSF 2.0, COBIT 2019, and practical reporting tools to create a risk scorecard, incident oversight checklist, and governance action plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for senior leaders with governance, assurance, risk, or executive responsibility for cybersecurity, privacy, and digital resilience. It is particularly relevant when you review management reporting or challenge investment and incident-readiness decisions. This course is designed for: Board directors who challenge cyber risk appetite and management reporting. Non-executive directors who scrutinize cyber controls and incident readiness. Permanent secretaries who oversee digital service resilience and cyber accountability. Public-sector regulators who assess cyber governance evidence and supervisory responses. Chief information security officers who brief boards on cyber exposure. Chief risk officers who integrate cyber risks into enterprise risk registers. Data protection officers who report privacy risks and response readiness. Internal audit executives who review cyber assurance plans and findings. Executive committee members who prioritize cyber investment against operational risks. Business continuity executives who align cyber recovery plans with service priorities.
prerequisites: Recommended: experience in board, executive, public-sector leadership, risk, audit, or cybersecurity oversight. No coding or technical configuration is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access if you want to work directly with the scorecard exercise.
